source_text: Ἐμοὶ δὲ δοκοῦσιν οἱ τοιοῦτοι πρῶτον μὲν τὴν τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος καὶ διοικοῦντος τόδε τὸ πᾶν ἀγνοεῖν δύναμίν τε καὶ σοφίαν, ἑκάστου ζώου φύσει καὶ γένει τὴν προσφυῆ καὶ κατάλληλον συναρμόσαντος τροφήν, καὶ μήτε πᾶσαν φύσιν πρὸς ἕνωσιν ἢ κρᾶσιν παντὸς σώματος ἰέναι δικαιώσαντος μήτε πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἑνωθέντων ἀπόρως ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῇ καθ᾿ ἕκαστον φύσει τῶν γενομένων τὸ δρᾶν ἢ πάσχειν ἃ πέφυκεν ἐπιτρέποντος, ἄλλοτε καὶ κωλύοντος, καὶ πᾶν ὃ βούλεται καὶ πρὸς ὃ βούλεται συγχωροῦντος ἢ μεταστρέφοντος· πρὸς δὲ τοῖς εἰρημένοις μηδὲ τὴν ἑκάστου τῶν τρεφόντων ἢ τρεφομένων ἐπεσκέφθαι δύναμίν τε καὶ φύσιν. Ἦ γὰρ ἂν ἔγνωσαν ὅτι μὴ πᾶν ὃ προσφέρεταί τις ὑπενδόσει τῆς ἔξωθεν ἀνάγκης, τοῦτο γίνεται τῷ ζώῳ τροφὴ προσφυής· ἀλλὰ τὰ μὲν ἅμα τῷ προσομιλῆσαι τοῖς περιπτυσσομένοις τῆς κοιλίας μέρεσι φθείρεσθαι πέφυκεν, ἐμούμενα τε καὶ διαχωρούμενα καὶ τρόπον ἕτερον διαφορούμενα, ὡς μηδὲ κατὰ βραχὺ τὴν πρώτην καὶ κατὰ φύσιν ὑπομεῖναι πέψιν, ἤ που γε τὴν εἰς τὸ τρεφόμενον σύγκρασιν· ὡσπεροῦν οὐδὲ πᾶν τὸ πεφθὲν καὶ τὴν πρώτην δεξάμενον μεταβολὴν τοῖς τρεφομένοις μορίοις προσπελάζει πάντως, τινῶν μὲν κατ᾿ αὐτὴν τὴν γαστέρα τῆς θρεπτικῆς δυνάμεως ἀποκρινομένων, τῶν δὲ κατὰ τὴν δευτέραν μεταβολὴν καὶ τὴν ἐν ἥπατι γινομένην πέψιν διακρινομένων, καὶ πρὸς ἕτερόν τι μεταχωρούντων ὃ τὴν τοῦ τρέφειν ἐκβέβηκε δύναμιν· καὶ αὐτῆς γε τῆς ἐν ἥπατι γινομένης μεταβολῆς οὐ πάσης εἰς τροφὴν ἀνθρώποις χωρούσης, ἀλλ᾿ εἰς ἃ πέφυκε περιττώματα διακρινομένης· τῆς τε καταλειφθείσης τροφῆς ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐσθ᾿ ὅτε τοῖς τρεφομένοις μέρεσι καὶ μορίοις πρὸς ἕτερόν τι μεταβαλλούσης, κατὰ τὴν ἐπικράτειαν τοῦ πλεονάζοντος ἢ περιττεύοντος καὶ φθείρειν πως ἢ πρὸς ἑαυτὸ τρέπειν τὸ πλησιάσαν εἰωθότος.
thought_title: God's power and the natural limits of food
orientation: Athenagoras is answering critics who say resurrection is impossible because bodies eaten by other people or animals become part of the eater's body.
pass_a_gloss: But to me such people seem first of all to be ignorant of the power and wisdom of the one who created and governs this whole universe, who fitted to each animal's nature and kind the food proper and suitable to it, and who judged it right neither that every nature should go toward union or blending with every body nor that he should be at a loss for the separation of the things that had been united, but who also permits to the nature of each of the things that have come to be to do or suffer what it is naturally disposed to do or suffer, at one time also preventing it, and who allows or turns aside everything that he wishes and toward what he wishes; and in addition to what has been said, they have not examined the power and nature of each of the things that nourish or are nourished. For otherwise they would have known that not everything that someone takes in under the pressure of external necessity becomes food proper to the animal; but some things are naturally disposed to be destroyed as soon as they come into contact with the parts of the stomach that enfold them, being vomited up and passed through and carried off in another way, so as not to endure even briefly the first and natural digestion, let alone the blending into the thing being nourished; just as indeed not everything that has been digested and has received the first change approaches the parts being nourished in every case, since some things are separated off from the nutritive power in the stomach itself, and others are separated off during the second change and the digestion that takes place in the liver, and pass over to something else which has gone beyond the power of nourishing; and indeed not all of the change that takes place in the liver itself goes toward food for humans, but it is separated off into the waste products that it is naturally disposed to become; and the food that is left behind in the very parts and members being nourished sometimes changes into something else, according to the dominance of what is in excess or superabundant and is accustomed somehow to destroy or to turn toward itself what has come near.

choices.term: τὴν τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος καὶ διοικοῦντος τόδε τὸ πᾶν ἀγνοεῖν δύναμίν τε καὶ σοφίαν
choices.english: to be ignorant of the power and wisdom of the one who created and governs this whole universe
choices.why: Keeps the two participles as coordinate attributes of God and preserves the object 'power and wisdom' as the thing unknown, matching the Greek word order and emphasis.
rejected: to fail to recognize the power and wisdom of the creator and governor of this universe

choices.term: τὴν προσφυῆ καὶ κατάλληλον συναρμόσαντος τροφήν
choices.english: fitted to each animal's nature and kind the food proper and suitable to it
choices.why: Renders the two adjectives as a pair describing the food, and keeps 'fitted' as the main verb of the participial clause, preserving the sense that God matched food to each creature.
rejected: adapted the appropriate and corresponding nourishment

choices.term: μὴ πᾶν ὃ προσφέρεταί τις ὑπενδόσει τῆς ἔξωθεν ἀνάγκης, τοῦτο γίνεται τῷ ζῴῳ τροφὴ προσφυής
choices.english: not everything that someone takes in under the pressure of external necessity becomes food proper to the animal
choices.why: Preserves the strong negation 'not everything' and the causal phrase 'under the pressure of external necessity' as the condition under which something is taken in, matching the Greek structure.
rejected: not all that is offered by external compulsion becomes suitable food

choices.term: ὡς μηδὲ κατὰ βραχὺ τὴν πρώτην καὶ κατὰ φύσιν ὑπομεῖναι πέψιν
choices.english: so as not to endure even briefly the first and natural digestion
choices.why: Keeps the consecutive force of 'so as not to' and renders 'κατὰ βραχύ' as 'even briefly' to convey the minimal degree, with 'first and natural' as a pair describing the digestion.
rejected: so that they do not even briefly undergo the first natural digestion

choices.term: κατὰ τὴν ἐπικράτειαν τοῦ πλεονάζοντος ἢ περιττεύοντος
choices.english: according to the dominance of what is in excess or superabundant
choices.why: Renders 'ἐπικράτειαν' as 'dominance' to convey the controlling power, and keeps the two participles as alternatives describing the prevailing element.
rejected: by the prevalence of the surplus or excess

pass_b_english: It seems to me that such people are, first of all, ignorant of the power and wisdom of the one who created and governs this whole universe. He fitted to each animal's nature and kind the food proper and suitable to it. He did not ordain that every nature should proceed to union or blending with every body, nor is he at a loss when it comes to separating what has been united. Instead, he permits each created thing's nature to do or undergo what it is naturally fitted for, while at other times he restrains it, and he allows or redirects everything he wills toward whatever end he wills.

Beyond these points, they have also failed to examine the power and nature of each thing that feeds or is fed. If they had, they would have known that not everything someone takes in under the pressure of external necessity becomes food proper to the animal. Some things, as soon as they come into contact with the folds of the stomach, are naturally destroyed, vomited up, passed through, or expelled in some other way, so that they do not endure even briefly the first and natural digestion, let alone the blending into the one being fed.

Likewise, not everything that has been digested and undergone the first change necessarily approaches the parts being nourished. Some things are separated out by the nutritive power in the stomach itself, while others are separated during the second change and the digestion that takes place in the liver, and they pass over to something else that has gone beyond the power of nourishing. And not all of the change that takes place in the liver itself proceeds to become food for humans; rather, it is separated into the waste products it is naturally fitted to produce.

Moreover, the food that remains in the very parts and members being nourished sometimes changes into something else, according to the dominance of what is in excess or superabundant, which is accustomed to corrupt in some way or turn toward itself whatever approaches it.

last_rejected.why: Source says 'toward whatever he wills,' not 'whatever end he wills'; the 'end' gloss is imported.
last_rejected.ruling: πρὸς ὃ βούλεται = 'toward what/which he wills'; 'end' is interpretive but within normal range of πρός + relative.

last_rejected.why: Neuter singular refers to the animal/thing fed, not 'one'; breaks Greek idiom.
last_rejected.ruling: 'One being fed' adequately renders τὸ τρεφόμενον; neuter singular as 'one' is acceptable English, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: which is accustomed to corrupt in some way or turn toward itself whatever approaches it
last_rejected.source_quote: φθείρειν πως ἢ πρὸς ἑαυτὸ τρέπειν τὸ πλησιάσαν εἰωθότος
last_rejected.why: Subject misidentified: 'what is in excess' corrupts/assimilates what approaches, not vice versa.
last_rejected.fix: which tends somehow to corrupt or assimilate to itself whatever approaches it
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly attributes action to 'what is in excess' (τοῦ πλεονάζοντος... εἰωθότος); 'which' refers to it, not the approaching thing.

polish.changed: Replaced 'enfolding parts of the stomach' with 'folds of the stomach' for clarity and natural modern usage, while preserving all claims and qualifications exactly.

notes.why: 'Enfolding' is an unusual rendering; 'folds' is standard.
